statements.label: asm:support
statements.title: Mutual Policy Support
statements.review_note: Assumption alignment only, not a proof that actual training satisfies it. For nonnegative normalized masses, equal zero sets match equivalent positivity; the finite change-of-measure and KL proofs require this support condition. Lean divides by zero as zero off support, while paper permits ratio one there; all cited expectations weight those terms by zero. Sampled positive-support identities agree.

statements.label: def:adaptive-norm
statements.title: Adaptive Normalization
statements.review_note: Consolidated unchanged ideal definition: nonempty active sign sets, excluded zero tokens, positive sums S+/S-, square sums Q+/Q-, count d. The two empirical moment constraints are written directly as alpha*S+=beta*S- and alpha^2*Q+ + beta^2*Q-=d. Existing finite_scaled_moments converts between these and token moments; adaptive_closed_form and adaptive_closed_form_unique prove same positive solution. Equation label preserved; numerical safeguards and empty-class fallback remain separate.

statements.label: def:impl-surrogate
statements.title: Trajectory-Level Surrogate
statements.review_note: Definition of the raw unclipped, unnormalized population trajectory surrogate. Baseline law and rollout law are fixed; conditional independence factors baseline from the entire response and permits integrating it to its prompt mean. Context weights can include a predictable action mask (EOS-emitting action active, subsequent shared absorbing padding inactive). Action-dependent prefix gate, normalization and random token-batch denominator are not included in this definition. Listed lemmas validate its finite conditional-law interpretation; the definition itself is not an empirical performance theorem.

statements.label: def:max-div
statements.title: Uniform Token-Level Divergence Bounds and Expected Per-Position TV
statements.review_note: Corrected unjustified attained maxima over unrestricted prompt/context sets to explicit finite nonnegative uniform upper bounds, matching the existing hTV and hKL theorem premises. All histories before the horizon and all prompts of the model are covered; finite context sets permit maxima. Expected local TV is weighted by rollout visitation, with family_adaptive_cost proving the finite prompt aggregation. No inference that mutual support supplies a uniform KL bound over arbitrary prompts.

statements.label: thm:adaptive-bound
statements.title: Finite-tree reward error bound
statements.review_note: Finite normalized history trees and finite prompt mixture; bounded reward B>=0, mutual support, uniform local TV and KL(rollout||current) bounds before horizon. Adaptive uses conditional sequence TV via product telescoping under rollout prefix occupancy, then the minimum of one, remaining-horizon local TV, and chain-rule Pinsker. Its coefficient is 4B*localTV*futureCap with Lean k=t-1 and N-1-k=T-t. Mixed independently uses performance_difference, the 2B*min(1,epsilon) gain bound, bounded-function expectation differences and contraction from full-response TV to marginal prefix TV. family_reward_error_bound takes the minimum of two valid absolute reward-error bounds after averaging over the same prompt law. Full-response TV is not substituted for conditional continuation TV; no token independence or automatic cached-gate guarantee. Expanded appendix derivations cite DPPO B.1-B.2 and TRM Adaptive/Mixed techniques as borrowed results. No new paper environment.

statements.label: thm:prefix-reentry-moment
statements.title: Retained-weight moments and lower-side reentry
statements.review_note: Paper time t corresponds to Lean prior-history depth n=t-1. The prefix log product is logRatioTrace on supported paths. The residual now includes only previous histories below the lower log threshold and an accepted current token. lower_safe_retained_moment_bound proves the retained-token envelope and uses conditional probability normalization; retained_moment_lower_reentry_bound integrates it over histories. The horizon result now assumes this smaller residual bound. upper_reentry_token_bound supplies the separate upper-excursion observation. lower_reentry_le_all_reentry proves the new uniform C+Rminus bound is no larger than the former C+Rall bound; no pointwise comparison with the former probability-refined expression is claimed. Gates are binary, so one gate in the local moment equals its square. EOS uses the full padded-tree gate: active implemented coefficients agree there, and their unconditional squared moment is dominated by the full-tree moment. Not a survival-conditioned moment or full-gradient variance bound. Retained-mass refinement: localRetainedMass is sum_a p(a|h)*M(h,a)*w(h,a), not the unweighted acceptance probability. It is nonnegative and at most one by conditional normalization (zero rollout mass handled separately). The local envelope bounds the second moment by C times this first moment. Averaging controlled histories and dropping their restriction only in a nonnegative first-moment term yields E[(Mw)^2]<=C*E[Mw]+R_lower. retained_moment_lower_reentry_bound now derives the former C+R_lower bound from the stronger result. Index n=t-1 and full-tree EOS convention unchanged; the active coefficient remains bounded by the full-tree moment. No new hypothesis and no full-gradient variance claim. The duplicate consecutive-acceptance proof now calls the shared envelope lemma. Two-policy revision: prefix results use rho=q/p; on-policy Max statements require accepted masks without an extraneous clipping premise. Generic finite identities retain their original mathematical assumptions.
